title: Customer-driven region scouting and conditional provisioning playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket defines a pragmatic playbook for 'scouting' customer requests for new region availability or strict data-residency constraints and the conditional provisioning workflow. The goal is to create a repeatable, sales-friendly triage that balances enterprise risk, legal/regulatory obligations, commercial opportunity, and engineering cost. This playbook is intended to sit upstream of a formal region onboarding project and to produce a single recommended outcome per request: Approve (fast-track), Approve with gating (pilot or limited capacity), Defer (collect more evidence), or Reject (legal/regulatory blocker).
acceptance_criteria: Intake form version v1 published and linked in sales handoff template
Triage rubric with weighted scoring (risk/opportunity/effort) published and used on 10 sample requests
Decision matrix and communication templates created for Approve / Pilot / Defer / Reject outcomes
Operational handoff checklist (quota requests, infra runbook, contact list) verified with ENG and Infra
Stakeholder sign-off from Legal, Security, and Sales for the playbook wording
steps: 1) Intake: Sales or CSM submits region request via standardized form (customer details, data residency constraint, expected QPS, revenue ARR, contract timeline, regulatory citation)
2) Triage: PM owner kicks off 48-hour triage using scoring rubric (see scoring_weights). Include immediate blockers from Legal or Security.
3) Outcome proposal: PM recommends Approve / Approve with gating / Defer / Reject and contacts stakeholder champions.
4) Technical feasibility check: ENG provides preliminary capacity estimate, expected latency delta, and approximate cost delta within 5 business days for non-blocked requests.
5) Commercial & contracts: Sales/legal define any contract language required for residency commitments and proposed SLAs.
6) Provisioning plan: For Approve or Pilot, create conditional provisioning runbook with rollback/fallback region and monitor dashboards.
7) Communication: Use prewritten templates to notify customer, internal stakeholders, and post-implementation runbook owners.
8) Post-mortem / review: After pilot or onboarding, collect metrics (latency, cost, error-rate) and update the rubric weights if necessary.
sample_cases: Case A — EU bank with PSD2 plus explicit contract clause requiring EU-only processing: Score=High regulatory_urgency + High ARR -> Recommend Approve with gating, require Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC and KMS integration

Case B — Startup headquartered in APAC asking for regional failover for latency reasons (no residency constraint): Score=High customer_size moderate technical_effort -> Recommend Pilot in single AZ capacity-limited pool, measure latency improvements and cost delta before full provision

Case C — SMB customer requesting single-country residency but low ARR and no contractual requirement: Score=Low ARR + Medium effort -> Recommend Defer and offer documented fallback (data minimization and IP allowlist) while collecting usage telemetry
notes: Trade-offs: Fast-tracking a region for a single enterprise customer increases cost and operational burden; ensure contractual cost-offsets (one-time onboarding fee or committed spend) are discussed with Sales.

Edge case: If Legal determines a country-level prohibition (data residency law prohibits cross-border transfer), the decision should default to Reject unless a private on-prem or approved local cloud partner is feasible.
We should avoid creating permanent per-customer forks in infra; prefer gated pilots and templated infra blueprints that can be reused across customers to amortize cost.
Operational constraint: Dedicated pools require a minimum commit of GPUs; estimate communicated cost must include projected utilization to avoid surprise spend.
